purpose: Replace ai-youtube 4-9 questions whose stems or objective metadata belonged to the displaced objective sequence. Question IDs, five-question structure, 20-point weights and attempt lifecycle are unchanged.

questions.question: A synthetic narration mispronounces a product name and stresses a figure incorrectly. What should the producer do before publishing?
options: Correct the pronunciation and emphasis, then listen to the whole take again
Add captions that contain the right spelling and publish unchanged
Lower the music so the error is harder to notice
Publish because the voice sounds natural overall
questions.answerRationale: Synthetic narration still needs a human listen and correction pass for names, numbers and meaning before it represents the video.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit pronunciation and review checks for synthetic narration; natural-sounding audio is not automatically accurate audio.

questions.question: Music is masking consonants in the narration. Which fix best serves the audience?
options: Raise the music so the video feels more energetic
Lower the music under the voice and check intelligibility on phone speakers
Remove all narration and rely on captions
Speed up the narration to finish before the music
questions.answerRationale: Narration must remain intelligible; ducking the music and testing on realistic playback devices is the direct fix.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit the narration-versus-music balance and test the mix on a small speaker.

questions.question: You want a synthetic voice that sounds like a recognisable actor. What is the responsible first step?
options: Use it because voice cloning tools are widely available
Check consent, rights and platform impersonation rules before using a recognisable voice
Pitch the voice down slightly and treat it as a different person
Only disclose the clone in a comment after publishing
questions.answerRationale: A recognisable person's voice raises consent, rights and impersonation risks that must be resolved before production.
questions.learningObjective: Choose between recorded and synthetic narration
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit the consent, rights and disclosure constraints for synthetic voices.

questions.question: Your recorded narration peaks into clipping. What should you change?
options: Compress the clipped track until the peaks disappear
Lower the input gain, record a test and keep peaks below clipping
Add a limiter and ignore the distorted sections
Record the same take twice and average the noise
questions.answerRationale: Clipping destroys information; the input gain must be corrected at capture, with a monitored test take.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit gain staging and test recording before the full take.

questions.question: Which evidence best shows that the final audio is ready to publish?
options: The waveform looks full in the editor
A full listen on phone and speakers, with levels checked and captions matching the audible words
The synthetic voice generated without an error message
The file exports at the highest available bitrate
questions.answerRationale: A real playback check plus level and caption verification tests the learner-facing result, not just the file settings.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit the final audio review checklist.

questions.question: A script explains how a request moves through three systems. Which visual is most appropriate?
options: A generic AI-generated image of glowing servers
A labelled diagram that accurately shows the three systems and their connections
A stock video of a person typing, reused for every section
A generated image with invented labels that look technical
questions.answerRationale: The visual must explain the actual process accurately; generic or invented imagery can mislead even when it looks professional.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit matching each visual to the claim it must support.

questions.question: A generated graphic contains a false label in an educational video. What should the editor do?
options: Keep it because viewers rarely read small labels
Correct or replace the graphic, then verify the final image against the source
Blur only the label and keep the rest of the graphic
Add a caption saying the graphic may be inaccurate
questions.answerRationale: A false label changes the claim; it must be corrected or replaced and the corrected visual verified.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit factual verification of generated visuals.

questions.question: A production reuses the same generated B-roll across several uploads. What makes each video valuable?
options: Saving each file with a different filename
Original context, explanation and relevance that add value beyond the shared footage
Changing the thumbnail colour for each upload
Using the footage for a longer duration in each video
questions.answerRationale: Reuse alone is not transformation; each video needs original context and value for its audience.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit originality and meaningful transformation.

questions.question: A realistic AI-generated scene depicts an event that never happened. What should the producer assess?
options: Only whether the image is high resolution
Whether using it would mislead, whether disclosure is required and whether rights and platform rules allow it
Only whether the scene is visually attractive
Whether the file size is small enough to upload
questions.answerRationale: Realistic synthetic depictions raise accuracy, disclosure, rights and platform-policy questions before use.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit realistic synthetic media and disclosure decisions.

questions.question: Which is the strongest review of a visual plan before editing begins?
options: Confirm that every image was generated by the same tool
Storyboard each claim, verify source and rights, and check labels, contrast and legibility on a phone
Count how many visual assets the plan contains
Choose the most colourful option for every section
questions.answerRationale: A visual plan is ready when each asset supports a claim, is lawful and remains readable on the target device.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit visual planning and accessibility checks.

questions.question: An AI-assisted cut removes a pause but also removes the word "not" from a key sentence. What should the editor do?
options: Keep it because the pacing is better
Restore the word and check the surrounding meaning against the transcript
Add a caption that contains the missing word
Replace the sentence with a shorter claim
questions.answerRationale: Pacing edits must not invert meaning; the editor must restore the word and verify the sentence in context.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit meaning-preserving review after automated cuts.

questions.question: Captions overlap a face and a key on-screen figure. What is the best fix?
options: Make the captions smaller but leave them in place
Reposition or shorten the captions, then check readability at the final size
Remove captions for the affected section
Move the face instead of the captions
questions.answerRationale: Captions must remain readable without covering the evidence or speaker; repositioning or shortening is the direct fix.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit caption placement and legibility checks.

questions.question: An edit has fast cuts, but retention drops when the main idea is explained. What is the most useful revision?
options: Add more cuts to increase energy
Clarify the explanation with a slower beat, a visual or a concrete example
Remove the explanation entirely
Add louder music under the explanation
questions.answerRationale: Retention loss at an explanation usually calls for clarity and support, not more pacing pressure.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit pacing decisions against comprehension.

questions.question: Which use of AI in editing keeps the human in control of the result?
options: Accept every automatic cut without reviewing it
Use AI for a rough cut or transcript, then review continuity, accuracy and captions yourself
Let the tool choose the final export settings unseen
Publish the first automated assembly as the final edit
questions.answerRationale: AI can accelerate assembly, but the editor remains responsible for meaning, continuity and the delivered file.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit the review boundary for AI-assisted editing.

questions.question: What is the strongest final check before uploading the edit?
options: Confirm the project file saved without an error
Watch the exported file with captions and audio, and verify facts, rights and platform specifications
Check that the timeline contains at least one transition
Confirm the edit used the newest AI feature
questions.answerRationale: The exported learner-facing file must be reviewed for meaning, captions, audio and platform fit, not just saved.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit the final export review checklist.

questions.question: A video has high impressions but low click-through rate. What should be investigated first?
options: The thumbnail and title promise against the audience and competing results
The video's total duration
The number of tags in the description
The upload time alone
questions.answerRationale: Impressions with weak clicks point first to packaging: whether the thumbnail and title earn attention from the right audience.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit the impressions-to-click path and packaging diagnosis.

questions.question: A thumbnail is viewed on a small phone screen. What should be checked?
options: Whether it contains enough small text to explain the video
Whether the subject, contrast and key text remain legible at phone size
Whether it uses at least five colours
Whether the file is larger than 2 MB
questions.answerRationale: Thumbnails are usually seen small; legibility, contrast and a clear subject matter more than detail or colour count.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit thumbnail legibility at realistic display size.

questions.question: An experiment changes the title, thumbnail, opening and video length at once. What is the main problem?
options: The experiment is too cheap to run
You cannot tell which change caused the result
The video will automatically be demonetised
The thumbnail will not render on mobile
questions.answerRationale: Changing several variables at once confounds the result; packaging tests should isolate a meaningful change.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit controlled packaging experiments.

questions.question: A thumbnail wins clicks, but viewers leave because the video does not deliver the promise. What should change?
options: Make the thumbnail even more sensational
Align the opening and content with the promise, or change the packaging to match the actual video
Hide the retention data
Add more tags to the description
questions.answerRationale: Clickbait that is not delivered harms trust and retention; the promise and the content must agree.
questions.learningObjective: Align the opening with the promise
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit the relationship between packaging and the opening.

questions.question: Which packaging test gives the cleanest evidence?
options: Change the title, thumbnail and traffic source together
Change one packaging element across comparable videos and compare the same metric
Ask three friends whether they like the new thumbnail
Pick the thumbnail with the most colours
questions.answerRationale: A useful test isolates a change and compares a defined metric across comparable conditions.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit controlled experimentation for packaging.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a publishing checklist?
options: To make the upload take longer
To verify metadata, visibility, captions, rights and the live result before and after publishing
To guarantee the video will go viral
To replace the need for a thumbnail
questions.answerRationale: A checklist catches avoidable publishing errors and confirms what the audience will actually see.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit the publishing verification checklist.

questions.question: What makes a description useful to viewers?
options: A long list of unrelated keywords
A clear summary, relevant sources and chapters or links that help navigation
The same paragraph copied into every upload
Only a request to like and subscribe
questions.answerRationale: Descriptions should help viewers understand and navigate the video; keyword stuffing does not serve that goal.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit viewer-facing metadata rather than keyword volume.

questions.question: Which promotion plan respects the audience and platform rules?
options: Post the link repeatedly in unrelated communities
Share it where the topic is relevant, disclose material AI assistance and avoid misleading claims
Buy engagement so the video ranks faster
Send unsolicited direct messages to strangers
questions.answerRationale: Responsible promotion targets relevant audiences and preserves disclosure and honesty.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit responsible promotion and disclosure.

questions.question: After upload, the video shows a processing or rights warning. What should the publisher do?
options: Publish anyway and ignore the warning
Resolve the warning or claim before promotion, then verify the public result
Delete the channel immediately
Re-upload the same file repeatedly until the warning disappears
questions.answerRationale: Warnings can affect availability or rights; they must be resolved before the video is promoted as live.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit the post-upload verification step.

questions.question: Which check best confirms that publishing succeeded?
options: The upload progress bar reached 100%
Open the live page as a logged-out viewer on mobile, and verify title, thumbnail, captions, visibility and links
The editor saved the project file
A scheduled post exists in the planner
questions.answerRationale: The audience-facing page is the real result; checking it logged out on a phone catches metadata, visibility and caption failures.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit live-page verification after publishing.

questions.question: A video has many impressions but few views. Which explanation should be tested first?
options: The video is too short
The thumbnail and title are not earning clicks from the audience being shown the video
The channel has too many subscribers
The audio bitrate is too high
questions.answerRationale: Impressions without views usually indicate a packaging or audience-fit issue, not duration or audio settings.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit the impressions-to-click diagnosis.

questions.question: Average view duration falls while impressions rise. What should the creator investigate?
options: Only the total number of uploads
Traffic sources, audience fit and the retention curve at the point where viewers leave
The colour of the channel banner
The number of hashtags in the description
questions.answerRationale: A changing impression mix can bring a different audience; retention by source and drop-off point diagnoses the cause.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit segmentation and retention-curve analysis.

questions.question: One video performs unusually well once. How should the channel use that result?
options: Treat it as proof of a repeatable formula
Treat it as a hypothesis, check the comparison period and test one related change
Delete the other videos because they underperformed
Copy the video exactly for every future upload
questions.answerRationale: A single result is weak evidence; it can suggest a hypothesis but needs comparison and a controlled test.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit sample size, baseline and causal caution.

questions.question: A report says a change improved subscribers, but gives no comparison period or tracking definition. What is missing?
options: A larger thumbnail
A baseline, a defined metric and a check for other changes that could explain the result
More AI-generated commentary
A longer upload schedule
questions.answerRationale: Without a baseline, definition and confounder check, the claim cannot support a causal decision.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit evidence standards for performance claims.

questions.question: Which combination best diagnoses the opening of a video?
options: Total subscribers and upload count
CTR alongside retention in the first 30 seconds and the audience's traffic source
The number of tags and the video file size
The channel's total watch time alone
questions.answerRationale: Opening performance is best read through the click path and early retention, segmented by where viewers came from.
questions.feedbackOnIncorrect: Revisit opening diagnosis using CTR and early retention.
